claim: Boot-counter saturation is implemented by suppressing the write once the counter sits at 1023, an off-by-one that also drops the legitimate 1024th byte (address 1023): it is acked and echoed but never written.
spec_ref: docs/architecture.md:Pipeline/LOAD (boot) -- "each pulse writes ui_in to the SRAM at an internal byte-address counter, then increments it (0-1023, the macro's full byte range)" and "A HOST_GO pulse at address 1023 writes/echoes that byte and stops advancing"; docs/isa.md:Data memory -- "It already streams the full 1024 bytes sequentially into the SRAM ... the second half is simply treated as data"

why_survives.directed: test_boot_echo_and_saturation streams 1026 bytes and checks the echo and that address 0 is not overwritten, but never reads data byte 1023 back; every other boot is a short program.
why_survives.random: fast_boot pokes the SRAM image directly; the per-byte LOAD handshake is out of the golden model's scope.
why_survives.board: Board images (program + .data) are far shorter than 1024 bytes, so address 1023 is never booted.
why_survives.formal: No props file constrains LOAD-mode SRAM writes; core_reset_props only allows host boot writes, it does not require them.
